These practicals are based on the online chapter [“Confounding adjustment using propensity score methods”](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/comparative-effectiveness/chapter_06.html), which complements the material in *Comparative Effectiveness and Personalized Medicine Research Using Real-World Data* (pp. 99–123). The book chapter is by Tammy Jiang, Gabrielle Simoneau, Changyu Shen, Fabio Pellegrini, and Carl de Moor.

The five practicals use the same simulated multiple-sclerosis cohort. Practical 1 estimates the propensity score and assesses baseline balance and overlap. Practicals 2–4 use propensity-score matching, stratification, and weighting; Practical 5 uses regression adjustment for the propensity score. All outcome analyses target the ATT, with optional ATE extensions at the end of each practical.

| Practical | Learner tasks | Worked solution |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline comparison and propensity-score estimation | [Task](chapter3_practical1_task.qmd) | [Solution](chapter3_practical1_solution.qmd) |
| Propensity-score matching | [Task](chapter3_practical2_task.qmd) | [Solution](chapter3_practical2_solution.qmd) |
| Propensity-score stratification | [Task](chapter3_practical3_task.qmd) | [Solution](chapter3_practical3_solution.qmd) |
| Propensity-score weighting | [Task](chapter3_practical4_task.qmd) | [Solution](chapter3_practical4_solution.qmd) |
| Regression adjustment for the propensity score | [Task](chapter3_practical5_task.qmd) | [Solution](chapter3_practical5_solution.qmd) |

All practicals use the same saved cohort, [`chapter3_ps_data.rds`](data/chapter3_ps_data.rds), generated by [`generate_chapter3_data.R`](generate_chapter3_data.R) from the supplied `generate_data()` simulator. The saved data have the same structure as the reference chapter and contain 10,000 simulated participants. Although the simulator's documentation says treatment is randomized, the implementation assigns treatment based on baseline covariates, so it is observational.

The sequence follows the linked [comparative-effectiveness chapter](https://smartdata-analysis-and-statistics.github.io/comparative-effectiveness/chapter_06.html). The exercises use `MatchIt`, `cobalt`, `dplyr`, and `marginaleffects` in R.
